page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text. Running head at the top, with the year 1638 and page number 169. Gathering signature "L 5" and catchword "piscopi" at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: dus monarchiæ pontificiæ , annotante Illyrico parte. 1. Clavis scriptura in voce, Episcopus. Rursus ibid. Hieronymus. Presbyteri sicut sciunt se ex ecclesiæ consuetudine esse subjectos ei qui sibi præpositus fuerit , ita Episcopi noverint, se magis consuetudine quam dominicæ dispositionis veritate presbyteris esse majores , & in commune debere ecclesiam regere. Ab Hieronymo ad Chrysostomum transeamus; Is hom. II. in 1. Tim. capit. 3. quærit, cur de Episcopis differens, omisso presbyterorum ordine, ad Diaconos transfilierit? Respondet. Quia medium (videlicet interveniens inter Episcopos & Diaconos) non multum, etenim illi (presbyteri) & docendi munus susceperant & præsidendi ecclesiæ, & quæ de Episcopis dixit eadem de presbyteris (dici.) sola enim horum electione ascenderunt; sensus est, Episcopos habere a presbyterorum electione quod ordinis causa præsint presbyterio, atque uni-ea [?] hac ratione a presbyteris differre: Eandem semitam terit Sedulius presbyter Scotus, qui eodem sæculo vixit quo Paladius, qui missus a Celestino pontifice Romano Episcopos in Scotia primus creasse dicitur, verba formalia Hieronymi citat & approbat, in expositione epistolarum ad Titum & Timotheum. Ambrosius eodem inclinat. in Comment. in 1. Timoth. cap. 3. Quare (inquit) post Episcopum Diaconatus ordinem subjecit? Nisi quia presbyteri & E-

page.notes: Page 169 of the 1638 printing, running head as printed. "uni-ea" at the line end is doubtful: the word may be "unica" or a printing error; marked [?]. "semitam" is read from the italic type and could be printed as "femitam"; I read it as the plain s form. The text ends on the half word "E-" (Episcopi), which continues on the next page with the catchword "piscopi".
